content:
watchOS 27 is coming soon, the next major software update for Apple Watch. I've been testing the watchOS 27 beta this summer, and there are three new features I particularly love.

#1: Brand New Home Screen View

In my opinion, Apple has never truly mastered the watchOS home screen design. The original honeycomb design looks decent in promotional images, and the later-added list view is my personal favourite, but both approaches can feel a bit awkward.

The problem is that Apple Watch is designed for extremely brief micro-interactions. And watchOS comes pre-loaded with tons of apps—not to mention third-party additions—making it quite inconvenient to find the one you want among a large collection of apps you never use.

watchOS 27 offers a solution: a dynamic app grid, which is the new default home screen view.

The dynamic app grid is similar to the honeycomb "grid view," but only displays your five most frequently used apps, plus the Siri app. Based on my experience, it almost always accurately shows the app I want to use. On the rare occasion it doesn't, you can still choose to open the full app view.

Most of the time, my watch face complications are my primary way of launching apps. But now the dynamic app grid serves as a handy secondary option for opening apps.

#2: Tap Gesture

Over the past few years, Apple has gradually introduced various novel and interesting gesture controls to watchOS.

Double Tap was the first gesture to appear, and last year saw the addition of Wrist Flick.

Now watchOS 27 introduces a third option: Tap. It's similar to Double Tap, but it's just a single tap and only works with Smart Stack.

When browsing Smart Stack, tap once with your index finger and thumb to select the highlighted widget. Essentially it's a convenient selection tool.

Now you can open Smart Stack, use Double Tap to browse, then use the new Tap gesture to select a widget and open the corresponding app.

#3: Siri AI

Siri AI is the focus of all Apple's new software this autumn, and watchOS 27 is certainly no exception.

Apple has rebuilt Siri from scratch for the AI era—a major upgrade.

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app, where you can browse all your conversations with the Siri assistant across all your devices. Importantly, the Apple Watch version of Siri is absolutely not a stripped-down, wrist-friendly lite version—it's identical to the Siri AI on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and so on.

According to Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering (via TechRadar), this is precisely what the Siri overhaul aims to achieve:

While other companies are still trying to build successful AI wearables, watchOS 27 will make the already popular Apple Watch one of them.

Which watchOS 27 features do you think are the best? Let us know in the comments section.
